name: Open Natural Turn
notes: Owner's description (2026-11-16): the box-turn-like figure after the Promenade Chassé. Steps as the box turn's forward half: forward on the right, side on the left, close the right (not the American-style open ending, which passes back on 3). The couple turns a quarter to the right from the line joining the partners, gradually across all three steps, and the partners turn to face each other on count 2; no rise. Three counts, ending in closed hold with another figure to follow. Named as the figure that takes a natural turn out of promenade; the closing on 3 is the owner's, as in the International Natural Turn. Turns: the couple's quarter is spread evenly, 30 degrees (1/12) a step; closing the V adds an eighth on count 2 (the lead right, the follow left). So the lead turns 1/12, 5/24 and 1/12 to the right (3/8 in all, from facing 315 to 90) and the follow 1/12 right, 1/24 left and 1/12 right (an eighth in all, from 225 to 270); they face each other from the end of count 2. Feet: the owner's rule is that the left foot stays to the left of the right foot except in explicitly crossed figures, and partners' feet keep 15 cm apart (both checked). On count 1 the lead's right foot takes a full stride (0.61) from behind to land 0.36 in front of his left, never across it (0.58 forward and 0.18 across from where it was, measured in his promenade facing); the chassé separates the partners slightly so the stride clears the follow's standing right foot (owner's request). On count 2 his left foot lands 0.4 to the side of his right once turned, then he closes. The follow goes 0.4 forward along the line of travel on her left, then her right lands to stay in hold, then she closes. History: the first version sent the lead's right foot 1.0 along the line of travel, crossing it in front of his left; a second crossed it less and curved the left foot round the front; both broke the left-stays-left rule, which the owner pointed out. Offsets to the millimetre where the closed-hold check needs them.
